title: An LSTM-Assisted MPC Framework for Smart Grid Load Management and Anomaly Monitoring
content: This study evaluates a forecast-informed, anomaly-aware model predictive con-trol (MPC) framework for flexible-load scheduling in a proposed ASKUE/KEGOC-oriented decision-support architecture. A univariate long short-term memory (LSTM) network generated 24-hour forecasts from 48-hour load histories, while a time-coupled optimizer enforced energy, power, and ramp-rate constraints. The evaluation used 4,380 measured-labelled hourly observations, with 648 held-out hours for scheduling. At the one-hour horizon, LSTM achieved RMSE = 0.224 kW, MAPE = 2.32%, and R² = 0.988. Under assumed flexible-load parameters, LSTM-MPC reduced the global peak by 13.21%, compared with 13.54% for seasonal-naive MPC, indicating no demonstrated scheduling advantage from LSTM forecasting. A matched AE-off/AE-on experiment then introduced identical measurement anomalies across five independently trained LSTM models. Autoencoder-triggered measurement repair using an independently retrained causal model increased mean global peak reduction from 8.70% to 12.89%. The mean paired improvement in 24-hour peak reduction was 1.077 percentage points (95% circular moving-block bootstrap interval: 0.436–1.946). All simulated schedules preserved energy and met modeled constraints. These findings support the feasibility of anomaly-aware scheduling in offline simulation, without es-tablishing physical closed-loop stability or operational deployment readiness.
